title: Colour-block scarf
subtitle: Two or three bold blocks of colour in a simple garter-stitch scarf.
excerpt: A garter-stitch scarf worked flat in two or three large colour blocks, knitted on 5 mm needles with aran yarn. Each colour is joined at a clean join and the tails are woven in. Finished dimensions are 20 cm wide by 175 cm long.
sourceNotes: Colour changes in flat knitting are described in Weldon's Practical Knitter for striped and banded scarves and shawls. Cornelia Mee, A Manual of Knitting and Crochet (1846), Internet Archive, covers colour joining techniques.
heroPrompt: A colour-block garter scarf laid flat showing three distinct colour sections: deep teal, warm cream, and rust orange, each approximately equal in length, with clean joins between them.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts x 36 rows = 10 x 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: The point where a new yarn colour is introduced. In flat knitting, joining at the start of a right-side row gives the neatest result. Leave a 15 cm tail of both the old and new yarn for weaving in.
A cast-on using the tail and working yarn together to form an elastic, neat edge.

content.text: This is a flat garter-stitch scarf worked from one short end to the other in three equal colour blocks, knitted on 5 mm needles with aran yarn, finishing at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long. Each colour block runs for approximately 58 cm (about 210 rows), and the joins are clean and woven in invisibly. Choose three colours that contrast well; solid tones or semi-solids work better than highly textured yarns at colour boundaries.

Flat construction was chosen because colour joins in flat knitting are simple: start the new colour at the beginning of a right-side row, leaving tails to weave in. No special technique beyond a clean join is needed. A
colour join
at the start of a row rather than mid-row keeps the join hidden inside the selvedge. The finished scarf uses about 65 g (117 m / 128 yards) of each colour, approximately 195 g total.
What you need

items.name: Aran-weight yarn, Colour A
items.substitutions: Any aran yarn. Solid or semi-solid works best at the colour joins.

items.name: Aran-weight yarn, Colour B
items.substitutions: Choose a colour that contrasts clearly with A and C.

items.name: Aran-weight yarn, Colour C
items.substitutions: For a two-colour scarf, use only A and B, each 97 g.

content.text: Gauge

18 sts x 36 rows = 10 x 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles, blocked. Each stitch off gauge changes the finished width by about 1.1 cm; each two rows off gauge across the full 630-row scarf adds or removes about 5 cm of finished length.
Stitches used
K (knit). Every row is a knit row.
Pattern
Cast on
Using Colour A and the
long-tail cast-on
, cast on 36 stitches. Tail length: (15.7 x 36) / 10 + 15 = about 72 cm.
Stitch count check-in: 36 stitches after the cast-on.
Body
Colour A block: K every row until the scarf measures 58 cm from the cast-on edge (approximately 210 rows). (36 sts)
Colour B join: at the start of a right-side row, drop Colour A (leave a 15 cm tail). Pick up Colour B, leaving a 15 cm tail. K to end. (36 sts)
Stitch count check-in at the colour join: still 36 stitches.
Colour B block: K every row until the scarf measures 117 cm from the cast-on edge (approximately 210 more rows). (36 sts)
Colour C join: as for Colour B join above.
Colour C block: K every row until the scarf measures 175 cm from the cast-on edge (approximately 210 more rows). (36 sts)
Cast off
Cast off using the standard method. Work loosely in Colour C.
Common faults

Visible jog at the colour join. A single horizontal step appears where the new colour begins. To minimise it, join at the start of a right-side row (not mid-row) and weave in the tails along the selvedge edge in the colour they match, not across the join.
Tails working loose. Weave each tail through at least five stitches and change direction once to anchor it. Split plied yarns work the needle through only one or two plies at a time for extra grip.
Unequal block lengths. Measure from the cast-on edge each time (not from the previous join) to avoid cumulative measuring error.
Finishing
Weave in all tails. For wool, wet block to even the tension and open the fabric.
Care
Handwash in cool water and lay flat to dry. Colour joins on garter stitch are stable after washing if the tails are well woven.
What to try next

The striped scarf uses narrower colour changes every ten rows for a classic stripe effect. Or try the mosaic colourwork scarf, which uses slip stitches to work two-colour patterns with only one colour per row.
